newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria prepares to reopen oil stations.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria prepares to reopen oil stations.

text.p: Oil flow stations shut at the weekend by Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit because of communal strife should reopen on Tuesday, a company official said.
"The teams have been assembling here this morning to go out and get everything started again," a senior Shell official in the midwestern oil town of Warri said by telephone from there.
"Full agreement has been reached with the local people for it to go ahead."
The flow stations involved are at Ogidigben, near Warri, the oil-producing city wracked by more than one month of communal clashes over the relocation of local council headquarters.

The closures forced Shell to shut in 20 percent or roughly 90,000 barrels per day (bpd) of the Forcados crude, causing the company to declare force majeure on some cargos of the blend due for lifting from April 29th.
Scores of lives have been lost in the conflict in Warri while Shell, the biggest oil operator in Nigeria has been forced to close several oil flow stations and to evacuate staff.
Oil accounts for more than 90 percent of Nigeria's foreign exchange income and last week the army deployed troops into Warri in an effort to stop the fighting.
